person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: Our main contribution is a thorough evaluation of networks of increasing depth using an architecture with very small (3 × 3) convolution filters, which shows that a significant improvement on the prior-art configurations can be achieved by pushing the depth to 16–19 weight layers.

span.label: convolutional network depth in large-scale image recognition
span.quote: In this work we investigate the effect of the convolutional network depth on its accuracy in the large-scale image recognition setting.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: Our implementation is derived from the publicly available C++ Caffe toolbox (Jia, 2013) (branched out in December 2013), but contains a number of significant modifications, allowing us to perform training and evaluation on multiple GPUs installed in a single system, as well as train and evaluate on full-size (uncropped) images at multiple scales (as described above).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: stack many very small (3x3) convolution filters to build very deep networks - depth (16-19 layers), not filter size, drives accuracy, while small filters keep parameters low and grow the effective receptive field
span.quote: a thorough evaluation of networks of increasing depth using an architecture with very small

span.label: Accuracy stops improving once depth reaches 19 layers on this dataset, so the depth benefit is shown to saturate.
span.note: what this limits: the depth claim on this dataset: THE ERROR RATE OF OUR ARCHITECTURE SATURATES WHEN THE DEPTH REACHES 19 LAYERS, BUT EVEN DEEPER MODELS MIGHT BE BENEFICIAL FOR LARGER DATASETS
span.quote: The error rate of our architecture saturates when the depth reaches 19 layers, but even deeper models might be beneficial for larger datasets.

span.label: The approach is computationally expensive: a single network takes weeks to train even on four high-end GPUs.
span.note: what this limits: anyone planning to reproduce or extend the training: ON A SYSTEM EQUIPPED WITH FOUR NVIDIA TITAN BLACK GPUs, TRAINING A SINGLE NET TOOK 2-3 WEEKS
span.quote: On a system equipped with four NVIDIA Titan Black GPUs, training a single net took 2–3 weeks depending on the architecture.

span.label: The depth result is licensed by a control: every other parameter was deliberately held fixed.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that depth improves accuracy: the authors fixed the other architectural parameters and increased depth alone, so the result holds for the family of configurations that control defines
span.quote: To this end, we fix other parameters of the architecture, and steadily increase the depth of the network by adding more convolutional layers, which is feasible due to the use of very small (3

span.label: The configurations being compared were built to one recipe, which is what makes the comparison fair and also what bounds it.
span.note: what this limits: a comparison between these networks and others: all the configurations compared here were designed using the same principles in order to isolate depth
span.quote: To measure the improvement brought by the increased ConvNet depth in a fair setting, all our ConvNet layer configurations are designed using the same principles

span.label: The explanation offered for faster convergence is labelled a conjecture by the authors.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that greater depth speeds convergence: the authors conjecture the nets required fewer epochs owing to implicit regularisation imposed by greater depth and smaller filters
span.quote: We conjecture that in spite of the larger number of parameters and the greater depth of our nets compared to (Krizhevsky et al., 2012), the nets required less epochs to converge due to (a) implicit regularisation imposed by greater depth

span.label: the conclusion - ABOUT REPRESENTATION DEPTH ON A CONVENTIONAL ARCHITECTURE: the paper's own summary is that depth is beneficial and that the state of the art can be reached with a conventional architecture substantially deepened, which is a narrower claim than 'deeper is better'
